To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) children who are unable to solve math problems often add correct problem-solving strategies to their repertoories when they are forced to gesture while explaining the solutions to those problems; (2) children are more receptive to instruction on the math problem when they are told to gesture while explaining a solution to the problem.

(a) children's implicit knowledge is revealed in gesture and is not revealed in speech; (b) when children gesture, they convey new and correct problem solving strategies; (c) when children gesture while explaining their solution to a novel task, their implicit knowledge is revealed and they are more receptive to instruction that enhances their performance; (d) when children gesture and are given instruction on a task, their performance on the task is improved.
telling children to gesture leads them to convey previously implicit ideas in gesture, which, in so doing enhances learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how children acquire knowledge and how this knowledge is expressed.
the role of gesture in learning and the role of instruction in learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, “Telling children to gesture encourages them to convey implicit ideas, which makes them receptive to subsequent instruction that leads to their learning.”
the study shows that the gesture can help children to convey their implicit knowledge.
, when children gesture while explaining a problem, they express their implicit knowledge, which, in so doing makes them receptive to new information that leads to learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gesture is not only a window into the mind, but also a tool for changing the mind.
making children gesture leads them to convey implicit knowledge in gesture, and this implicit knowledge can be made explicit through instruction.
children who are unable to solve a problem can be made to express their implicit knowledge in gesture, and this expression in gesture can be used to guide them to learn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gestures are a powerful window into the mind and that eliciting gestures can be a powerful learning tool.
children are not just passive recipients of instruction; they are active learners.
children are not just passive receivers of information.
